blocks.text: Setting up your podcast production workflow

Podcast production involves many moving parts. You handle guest outreach, script writing, show notes, and episode metadata. A centralized Google Doc acts as the source of truth for your team. Avoid keeping these documents scattered in your Finder. Create a folder structure in Google Drive that matches your production stages. Use a naming convention like YYYY-MM-DD_EpisodeTitle_Draft to keep files sorted by date.
Google Docs shortcuts for Mac efficiency

Speed matters when you are drafting show notes under a deadline. On your Mac, the Command key replaces the Control key found on other platforms. Memorize these essential shortcuts to keep your hands on the keyboard.

Using ⌘ + Option + 1 through 6 applies heading styles instantly. This is helpful for structuring your show notes with clear sections for intro, guest bio, and timestamps. Navigation is easier when you use Option + Left Arrow or Option + Right Arrow to jump between words.
Managing podcast guests in Google Docs

Guest management is a major non-audio time sink. Create a master document for each season. Use a table to track guest names, contact info, recording dates, and release status. This prevents you from losing track of who you need to email next.

blocks.text: Creating a reusable podcast show notes template

Do not write your show notes from scratch every time. Create a template document that contains your standard headers, episode intro boilerplate, and social media links. When you start a new episode, go to File > Make a copy. This keeps your formatting consistent across every release.
Handling long scripts and character limits

A single Google Doc supports up to 1.02 million characters. This is plenty for most podcast scripts. If your show is a long-form narrative, you might approach this limit. If you reach it, consider splitting your script into multiple documents, one for each act or episode segment.

You might need to write show notes while traveling. Google Docs supports offline editing. You must use the Google Chrome browser and install the Google Docs Offline extension. Once enabled, your recent documents become available without a connection. Your changes sync automatically once you are back online.

Collaboration is where Google Docs shines. Use the Suggesting mode for script reviews. This allows your team to propose edits without changing your original text. Right-click any word to add a comment or use ⌘ + Option + M. Use @mentions in comments to notify specific team members about tasks.

faq.question: Is there an official Google Docs app for Mac?
faq.answer: No. Google Docs is a web-based service. You access it through a browser like Chrome or Safari.

faq.question: How do I add a comment quickly in Google Docs?
faq.answer: Use the shortcut ⌘ + Option + M while your cursor is in the document.

faq.question: Can I edit my podcast scripts offline?
faq.answer: Yes, if you use Google Chrome and have the Google Docs Offline extension installed.

faq.question: What is the character limit for a Google Doc?
faq.answer: A single document can hold up to 1.02 million characters.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Google Docs?
faq.answer: Yes. You can hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur where a menu item is, or use it to dictate text directly into your document.
